intro: Sayings that Spanish speakers quote all the time, often only the first half.
p.no hay mal que por bien no venga: every cloud has a silver lining
p.no por mucho madrugar amanece más temp: rushing doesn't make things happen sooner
p.más vale pájaro en mano que ciento vol: a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush
p.a caballo regalado no le mires el dien: don't look a gift horse in the mouth
p.quien mucho abarca, poco aprieta: don't bite off more than you can chew
b1.texto:
A **refrán** packs advice into one line. People often say only the beginning and let you finish it: «Ya sabes, no por mucho madrugar…»

Their grammar is old and compact, and you now have the tools to read it.

- **No hay mal que por bien no venga**: a relative clause in the subjunctive after no hay.
- **No por mucho madrugar amanece más temprano**: por mucho + infinitive means however much you do it.
- **De tal palo, tal astilla**: no verb at all. From such a stick, such a splinter.
- **A caballo regalado no le mires el diente**: a negative command.
- **Más vale** X **que** Y: X is worth more than Y.
- **Quien mucho abarca, poco aprieta**: whoever takes on a lot, holds little tight.
b2.f0: I missed the train, but at the station I ran into an old friend.
b2.f1: Every cloud has a silver lining.
a4: that does not come for some good (subjunctive)
b2.f2: His son is just like him: he talks non-stop.
b2.f3: Like father, like son. And did you make it to the meeting?
b2.f4: An hour late. But better late than never.
b2.f5: Calm down, don't rush. You know: rushing doesn't make things happen sooner.
b4.pregunta: Your friend lost his job and then found a better one. Which proverb fits?
b4.o0.refuerzo: Something good came out of the bad.
b4.o2.refuerzo: That warns against taking on too much.
b5.pregunta: A girl is exactly like her mother. Which proverb fits?
b5.o0.refuerzo: The splinter is like the stick.
b6.pregunta: «Más vale pájaro en mano que ciento volando» advises you to…
b6.o0.refuerzo: One bird in the hand beats a hundred flying.
b6.o2.refuerzo: That is the idea of no por mucho madrugar amanece más temprano.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Madrugar is the infinitive: no por mucho madrugar.
b7.o1.refuerzo: After por mucho comes an infinitive, not a conjugated verb.
b7.o2.refuerzo: After por mucho comes an infinitive, not a participle.
b8.pregunta: You get a present you don't like. Which proverb tells you not to complain?
b8.o1.refuerzo: That means no sooner said than done.
b10.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (150–180 words).** Choose three proverbs and write a short situation that illustrates each one.

**Speak (about 3 minutes).** Explain aloud three proverbs from your own language and look for a Spanish equivalent.
